claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for?** If yes, how many children are you asking about?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child I'm asking about - my son Alex. He's 18 and I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 18, which is over 16, there are specific rules that apply. You can normally still qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 20 **and** they stay in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he attending college, sixth form, doing A-levels, or in approved training?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. Alex is doing his A-levels at college right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you! Since Alex is 18 and doing his A-levels at college, this counts as approved education.

Now I need to ask about your circumstances:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your relationship and responsibility for Alex:

**Does Alex live with you, or if he doesn't live with you, are you contributing at least the same amount as Child Benefit would pay towards his upkeep** (such as for food, clothes, or pocket money)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't live with me, but I do contribute towards his upkeep regularly - I help with his clothes, food, and things he needs for college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To clarify:

**Are you contributing an amount that is at least equal to what Child Benefit would pay?** 

For context, Child Benefit rates are currently around £25.60 per week for the eldest/only child, and £16.95 per week for additional children. So for one child, that would be approximately £102-£110 per month.

Are your contributions meeting or exceeding this amount?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I contribute about £26 a week towards Alex's upkeep, so that meets the requirement.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

Now I need to check a few more details about Alex's situation:

**Has Alex started any paid work for 24 hours or more per week, or is he receiving any benefits in his own right** (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't started any paid work like that, and he's not receiving any benefits in his own right.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, the person he's living with, or another parent/guardian?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. Just one final question:

**Are you already claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or would this be a new claim?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: This would be a new claim - I'm not currently claiming Child Benefit for him.

## Good News! You Are Eligible for Child Benefit for Alex

Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**. Here's why:

✓ **Alex is in approved education** - He's 18 and doing his A-levels at college, which qualifies as approved education. You can claim Child Benefit for children under 20 who are in approved education or training.

✓ **You're contributing to his upkeep** - Even though Alex doesn't live with you, you're contributing approximately £26 per week towards his upkeep (clothes, food, college needs), which meets the requirement of contributing at least as much as Child Benefit pays.

✓ **You live in the UK** - You meet the residency requirement.

✓ **No conflicts** - Alex isn't working 24+ hours per week, isn't receiving benefits in his own right, and no one else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

### What to do next:
You can now make a claim for Child Benefit for Alex. You'll need to apply through HMRC.

**Important reminder:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You might want to check if this applies to you.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about claiming Child Benefit?
